title: Write tests that catch bugs
summary: This time you write the tests. The grader plants bugs and checks that your tests catch them.
hints: Each bug only shows up with the right input. Write one test per behaviour: capital letters, a run of symbols, a very long title, and a title with nothing usable in it.
Every test method needs its own name starting with test_, such as test_lowercases. A method with a repeated name replaces the earlier one.
If test 2 fails, your expected value is wrong. Run make_slug(...) in the Console to see what the correct code really returns.
For a long title: slug = make_slug('word ' * 30), then self.assertLessEqual(len(slug), 50) and self.assertFalse(slug.endswith('-')).
For errors, put the call inside the block: with self.assertRaises(ValueError): and on the next, indented line make_slug('!!!').

quiz.question: Your tests pass against a buggy version of the code. What does that tell you?
options: The tests don't check that behaviour. There's a gap
quiz.explanation: This is the idea behind mutation testing: good tests fail when the code is wrong. A test that can't fail isn't protecting anything.

quiz.question: What's the usual shape of a unit test?
quiz.explanation: Set up the inputs, call the code once, then assert on the result. Keep each test focused on one behaviour.

quiz.question: Django's TestCase gives each test a clean database. How?
options: It wraps each test in a transaction and rolls it back
It uses a new server each time
quiz.explanation: The rollback keeps tests fast and independent, so they can run in any order.
